Put $\gamma(t)=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|$. For every transverse homogeneous solution $\mathbf b$ and $t_0\le t'\le t\le T$, assume $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$, and assume $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||\mathbf a|$ at the origin. Use the fixed smooth radial envelope $g$, equal to one on $|a|\le\ell_*$ and zero on $|a|\ge2\ell_*$, and the fixed one-periodic zero-mean phase profile $F_h$ of Section 3. The time cutoff $\widetilde\chi$ is smooth on $[0,T]$, lies in $[0,1]$, and is zero for $t<t_0$. This permits $\widetilde\chi\equiv1$ when $t_0=0$. On the centered label cell set $A_1=g\mathbf aF_h$, $V_1=\widetilde\chi A_1$ and $\mathsf p_1=\widetilde\chi\mathsf p[A_1]$, where $\mathsf p[A_1]$ has zero phase mean and $A_{1,t}+MA_1+\kappa\partial_s\mathsf p[A_1]=0$. Set $B_1= ar q_1=C_1=0$ and $C_{p+1}=C[V_p]$. Here $C[V]=\mathbf d	imes(-\kappa	imes\partial_s^{-1}V/|\kappa|^2)$, $\mathbf d=F^{-T}
abla_a$, and $\partial_s^{-1}$ is the zero-mean phase primitive. Higher transverse velocities have zero phase mean, are perpendicular to $\kappa$ and satisfy $V_p(0)=0$. The means have $B_p=Fz_{p,t}$, $\operatorname{div}_a z_{p,t}=0$ and $z_p(0)=z_p(T)=0$. Use the recursive sources in (5.27)–(5.28), including $-R_U\circ X$ at mean level two. Mean pressures have zero spatial mean and transverse pressures zero phase mean. The terminal convention is $V_{P+1}=B_{P+1}=0$. All profiles are smooth on $[0,T]$, one-periodic in phase, and satisfy $f(t,a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)=f(t,a,s)$ for $n\in\mathbb Z^3$.

atural$. The notation $f^
atural(t,x)$ means $f(t,a,k_*\cdot a)$ at $a=X(t,\cdot)^{-1}(x)$. Choose $C_{m step}=\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b$ sufficiently large and assume $C_{m step}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$. The exponent $b$ is independent of $P$, whereas $\Gamma_P$ may depend on $P$ and the fixed profiles.

Fix a smooth radial multiplier $\psi$ with $0\le\psi\le1$, $\psi=1$ on $|\xi|\le1$ and $\psi=0$ for $|\xi|>2$. For $\Lambda\ge1$, let $u=S_\Lambda V$, where the multiplier on $e^{2\pi i\xi\cdot x}$ is $\psi(\xi/\Lambda)$, and let $p$ be the periodic zero-mean solution of $\Delta p=-\operatorname{tr}((
abla u)^2)$. The formal statement supplies such $u,p$. It proves $u$ smooth, odd and divergence free, with Fourier support $|\xi|\le2\Lambda$, and proves its momentum residual $R_u=u_t+u\cdot
abla u+
abla p$ odd and divergence free, with support $|\xi|\le4\Lambda$.

Put $\varepsilon_\Lambda=\Lambda^{2-P}(1+\|V\|_{C_tC^{P,1/2}})^2$. The conclusions are $\|u-V\|_{C_tC^{2,1/2}}\le C_{2,P}\varepsilon_\Lambda$ and $\|R_u\|_{C_tC^{1,1/2}}+\|D^2(p-\Pi)\|_{C_tC^{0,1/2}}\le C\|R_V\|_{C_tC^{1,1/2}}+C_{2,P}\varepsilon_\Lambda$. They imply the stated upper quadratic-form bound $D^2(p-p_U)\le(C_{m step}\lambda^{-1/4}+C\|R_V\|_{C_tC^{1,1/2}}+C_{2,P}\varepsilon_\Lambda)I$. All time suprema are over $[0,T]$.

The exponent $2-P$ is an integer, so it is negative when $P>2$; it is not subtraction truncated at zero. The formal estimate for the sum permits the two terms to be evaluated at independent times. This represents the sum of two time suprema in (5.56), not a weaker bound at one common time. The multiplier is fixed before its constants are chosen, and those constants precede the parent, depth and cutoff frequency. The larger parent-pressure and seed classes remain admissible, but the new pressure $p$ is normalized by the Poisson equation exactly as in the paper. Existence is explicit; uniqueness of this normalized pressure follows from the periodic Poisson problem rather than an additional uniqueness clause in this numbered statement.
